title: Convex hull representations for bounded products of variables
contribution: Shows that the convex hull of {(x,y,xy)} over a box with upper and/or lower bounds on the product is RLT plus the bound(s) plus at most three SOC constraints (each valid on a subdomain), explicitly in (x,y,z), and uses closed-form hull volumes to analyse spatial branching on z.
problem_entry: Known hulls with bounds on z were an infinite lifted-tangent family needing separation (Belotti/Miller), complex and hard to specialise to lx=0 (Nguyen-Richard-Tawarmalani), or disjunctive in a lifted space (Santana-Dey); the target is an explicit SOC description in the original variables (pp. 2-3).
key_idea: Re-interpret the construction of lifted tangent inequalities: solve for the segment weight alpha as a function of (x,y) so that z <= alpha*lz + (1-alpha)*uz becomes one nonlinear constraint, then show it is SOC (pp. 3, 6); Props. 1-9 give the cases, with a globally valid center cone as a close approximation (pp. 7-24).
assumptions: 0 <= l < u, F' nonempty, rescaled so ux=uy=1 (p. 2); bound tightening lz <= lx,ly <= uz from Sec. 4 (pp. 2-3, 17); lxly < lz, and lx <= ly by symmetry, in Sec. 4.3 (pp. 20-21).
proof_devices: Known hull (RLT + bounds + lifted tangents) used as a black box; each proof shows the SOC implies all lifted tangents on its domain (pp. 7-12)
Quadratic equation for the mixing weight alpha, appropriate root substituted (pp. 9, 11-12, 19)
Radicand rewritten as a quadratic form with an explicit PSD 2x2 matrix M (p. 9)
Global validity of the center cone via (sqrt(uz)-sqrt(xy))(sqrt(xy)-sqrt(lz)) >= 0 (p. 12)
Symbolic congruence S Q S^T to a matrix with one negative eigenvalue gives SOC form (10) (p. 20)
Dissection of the (lx,ly) parameter space into regions A-F, with symmetry (pp. 20-22); Props. 6-9 stated with proofs omitted (pp. 21-22)
Closed-form volume integrals (7)-(8) (p. 15)
experiments: none (no computational study); 3-D hull figures, cross-sections (Fig. 7, p. 14) and volume curves: summed child-hull volume minimised near b ~ 0.2, about 32.4% reduction (pp. 15-17).
positioning: Builds on Belotti-Miller-Namazifar lifted tangents (p. 3); specific two-point contrast with Nguyen et al. and contrast with Santana-Dey's lifted disjunction (p. 3); volume comparison follows Anstreicher and Lee-Skipper-Speakman (pp. 4, 17).
writing: Proposition + 3-D figure per case, simple case (lx=ly=0) before general bounds; hedged empirical remarks ('empirically', 'It appears', 'We would expect', pp. 4, 14, 26); discovery route of (10) explained separately from the proof (p. 20).
limits_future: Some SOC pieces only locally valid, so an exact global form needs a disjunction or an approximation (p. 26); Props. 6-9 unproved in the text (pp. 21-22); future: multilinear n>2, bounds on xy in the 5-variable system, z = x^T y (p. 26).

method_links.note: Small recurring substructure (bilinear term with product bounds); explicit description in original variables rather than a lifted disjunction; results by parameter region
Empirical regularities hedged at their level, but Props. 6-9 printed with proofs omitted and no certificate or counterexample search

Prove SOC-representability via an explicit PSD quadratic form for the radicand (p. 9) or a symbolic congruence to one negative eigenvalue (p. 20)
Choose a spatial branching point by minimising the closed-form sum of child-hull volumes (pp. 15-16)
Check a hull approximation with cross-sections at several fixed values of the lifted variable (p. 14)

quotes.text: We do not use the inequalities per se, but rather show how the process by which they are constructed can be re-interpreted to generate nonlinear inequalities.
If α can be expressed as a function of (x, y) then the result is a single nonlinear constraint that is equivalent to a family of lifted tangent inequalities.

title: Strengthened SDP relaxation for an extended trust region subproblem with an application to optimal power flow
contribution: Derives a polynomial-time separable class of valid linear inequalities for the SDP relaxation of an extended TRS (hollow ball plus an SOC with identity Hessian) that strengthens Shor + KSOC, shows that Chen-Atamturk-Oren's OPF hull cuts are special cases, and gives locally valid SOC cuts for {x >= 0 : ||x|| <= 1}.
problem_entry: Extended TRS (1) is polynomially solvable (Bienstock) but has no known tight convex relaxation (p. 2); it arises in OPF; the paper was motivated by wanting to understand Chen et al.'s OPF cuts (fn. 2, p. 6).
key_idea: Combine SOC self-duality, the RLT-type product (R-||x||)(||x||-r) >= 0 written as an SOC membership, and nonnegative multipliers q(x), l(x); reduce the quartic to a quadratic with a constant lower bound on q+l and linearise (Thm. 1, pp. 6-9); separate by bootstrapping the dual cone of any current SDP relaxation (pp. 18-20).
assumptions: Ball and SOC share the identity Hessian (p. 2; limitation, p. 28); [c]max by binary search on a convexified subproblem (p. 7); full-dimensional F with a known interior point, so that separation is bounded (p. 19); OPF: L22 > 0, U12 > L12 (p. 14).
proof_devices: SOC self-duality inner product gives base cut (7) (p. 6)
Prop. 1: scaled SOC membership from (R-||x||)(||x||-r) >= 0 (p. 7)
Degree reduction of a quartic inequality by a constant lower bound [q+l]lowbd (Thm. 1, pp. 8-9)
Dominance by extremes via linearity in r-hat (Cor. 1, p. 9)
OPF equivalence via complex rotation and a 2-D polyhedral cone written as an SOC (Lemma 1, Props. 3-4, Thm. 2, pp. 13-16); algebra verified by Matlab code (fn. 3, p. 16)
Locally valid SOC cuts by minimising over the slab direction on sign domains D_IJ (Thm. 3, p. 17)
Bounded truncation of the dual cone via its recession cone (fn. 4, p. 19)
Numerical non-implication: negative minimum of the cut slack over Shor+KSOC (Examples 1-2, pp. 5, 17-18)
experiments: Matlab/CVX/MOSEK 9.1, single core (p. 21); 15,000 random instances per n = 2..10 in three cases, bootstrapped from Shor and from Shor+KSOC; exact = eigenvalue ratio > 1e4; gap closure vs best of 100 fmincon runs (pp. 22-23); cuts help most at low n, and from Shor+KSOC improve nothing for n >= 4 in the general case (p. 24); 110,000 extra n=2 instances, the 62 inexact ones all closed (p. 25); 100 filtered instances all closed by the local cuts (p. 26).
positioning: Builds on SOCRLT (Sturm-Zhang, Ye-Zhang, Burer-Anstreicher) and KSOC (Anstreicher), showing Shor+KSOC is the strongest baseline (p. 4); re-reads the Chen-Atamturk-Oren cuts as special cases (pp. 1, 11-16); names Lasserre multipliers as the analogy (p. 8); acknowledges Bienstock while stating a different goal (p. 2).
writing: Motivating one-line inequality and 2-D example before the theory (p. 5); code repository announced (p. 6); step-by-step separation example (pp. 20-21); 'rudimentary' implementation admitted (p. 22); regularities printed as labelled Conjectures 1-2 (pp. 25-26).
limits_future: Identity Hessian only (workaround sketched), weaker in higher dimensions, gap not closed for general F (pp. 24, 28-29); future: streamline separation, higher n, other applications, self-duality of other cones (p. 29).

title: A strengthened SDP relaxation for quadratic optimization over the Stiefel manifold
contribution: Adds a Kronecker-product LMI (the redundant LMI [I U^T; U I] >= 0 multiplied by itself and linearised) to the DiagSum SDP relaxation of quadratic optimization over the Stiefel manifold, and shows on four synthetic classes that it strengthens Shor and DiagSum substantially, except on block-diagonal instances, at much higher solve time.
problem_entry: QPS is NP-hard for general p (TRS for p=1); Gilman-Burer-Balzano's DiagSum was strong for block-diagonal H; the question is whether a further strengthening helps for general H (pp. 1-2).
key_idea: Ladder Shor <= DiagSum <= Kron: adapt DiagSum to general H via UU^T <= I, then take the Kronecker product of the implied LMI with itself and linearise to M(u,X) >= 0 (pp. 3-6); a Hadamard variant was found never to help (p. 7).
assumptions: n >= p; general H, g; block-diagonal class with g = 0, following [15] (fn. 1, p. 5; p. 9); no theorems beyond validity.
proof_devices: Schur-complement chain for UU^T <= I (p. 4)
Kronecker product of PSD matrices is PSD; explicit linearisation via the K_ji matrices (pp. 5-6)
Symmetric permutations give only a permuted constraint (p. 7)
Hadamard LMI is a principal submatrix of M, so its strength lies between DiagSum and Kron (p. 7)
Primal bound by polar-factor projection onto St(n,p) plus Manopt polishing, giving a two-sided gap (pp. 7-8)
experiments: Four classes (random, block-diagonal, Procrustes, Penrose), n in {6,9,12}, p in {2, ceil(n/2), n-1}, 1,000 instances per cell; solved = relative gap < 1e-4; MATLAB/Mosek 9.3.10/Manopt 7.0/YALMIP, one core (pp. 9-11); Kron takes up to 250 s vs 0.7 s for Shor (p. 11); Kron best on random instances, no gain on block-diagonal, nearly all solved on Procrustes/Penrose (p. 12); Gurobi dropped after a preliminary test (p. 8).
positioning: Builds on his own group's DiagSum [15] and Anstreicher's Kronecker constraints [4] (p. 2); Jiang-Li credited for the Hadamard idea (p. 7); global solver set aside on evidence (p. 8).
writing: Short; cost trade-off stated in the abstract (p. 1); contribution called an 'observation' (p. 3); unproven implication explicitly labelled (p. 7); losses stated in the introduction (p. 2).
limits_future: High solve time, no gain on block-diagonal H, a few Procrustes/Penrose instances unsolved (pp. 11-14); future: cheaper enforcement of the Kronecker LMI, prove or refute tightness on Procrustes/Penrose, extend the certificate of [15] (pp. 12-14).

method_links.note: Stack known relaxations and recombine an ingredient (Kronecker product of a redundant LMI), but on the whole problem, with no small-substructure hull

Unfiltered random pools, 1,000 per cell, no hard-pool engineering
Known theorem (Kronecker PSD) plus a known relaxation, tested computationally, with the theory left open

transferable: Multiply a redundant LMI by itself (Kronecker or Hadamard) and linearise in the lifted variable; test the cheaper Hadamard submatrix first (pp. 5-7)

Run a general global solver on one small cell with a time limit and state why it is excluded as a baseline (p. 8)

quotes.text: Our conceptual contribution in this paper is the observation that the Kronecker-product idea applies in this setting
Said differently, it appears that DiagSum implies (4), although we have so far not been able to prove this.

title: Convex Hulls in Quadratic Space
contribution: Encyclopedia entry that defines the (closed) quadratic hull conv{(x, xx^T) : x in F}, shows that QCQP is linear optimisation over it, and catalogues the special cases where it equals the Shor relaxation plus explicit RLT/SOC-RLT constraints.
problem_entry: Convexification of nonconvex problems and their substructures, by analogy with the integer hull; for quadratic objectives the relevant hull lives in (x, xx^T) space (pp. 1-2).
key_idea: QCQP = min Q.X + 2c^T x over C(F) (eq. (4), p. 2); an explicit C(F) is as hard as the QCQP, so the Shor relaxation S(F) is the standard outer approximation; the entry catalogues cases with C(F) = S(F) or S(F) + RLT/SOC-RLT (pp. 2-6).
assumptions: F nonempty (p. 3); compact F gives a closed C(F) (p. 2); case-specific conditions are named (two-sided Slater, A != 0, parallel or non-intersecting linear constraints, proper triangles/tetrahedra/quadrilaterals, boundary of H inside F) (pp. 3-6).
proof_devices: Reported, not proved: SOC-RLT construction by multiplying a linear slack into the ball SOC (p. 4)
RLT outer product (b-Ax)(b-Ax)^T >= 0 (p. 6)
Completely positive cone is SDP-representable for m <= 4, which gives the hulls of polytopes with at most four facets (p. 5)
One-line counterexample showing the alternative expression is needed when A = 0 (p. 4)
positioning: Neutral survey voice; Burer's own results (refs. 1-4, 15) listed alongside Sturm-Zhang, Xia et al., Pong-Wolkowicz, Jin et al. and Joyce-Yang without ranking (pp. 3-6).
writing: Easiest to hardest (one quadratic, ball + linear, only linear, non-intersecting), picture first (Fig. 1, p. 3), each case a displayed formula plus its condition; ends on an open-problem sentence (p. 6).
limits_future: Only a few cases have explicit quadratic hulls; novel techniques for strong valid inequalities are needed (p. 6).

method_links.note: QCQP packaged as linear optimisation over one convex object, the quadratic hull
Catalogue of small substructures whose hull is Shor plus explicit RLT/SOC-RLT pieces

transferable: Present hull results as 'hull = Shor + named extra constraints + condition for exactness', case by case (pp. 3-6)
Open with a 1-D example whose lifted hull can be drawn (pp. 2-3)
Pair a necessity claim with a one-line counterexample (p. 4)

quotes.text: In general, determining an explicit expression for C(F) or C(F) is at least as difficult as solving the corresponding QCQP.
Additional novel techniques are needed to generate strong valid inequalities for quadratic hulls.
